title: HfO2/SiO2 multi-cavity defect structure for sharp passband
scientific_hypothesis: Multiple defect cavities within the Bragg stack create a sharper, more rectangular passband in 255-280 nm compared to single-cavity designs, improving out-of-band rejection.
design_principle: Coupled cavity structures create multiple resonant modes that can be tuned to merge into a single broader passband with steeper edges. This improves the transition from pass to block regions.
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 14 layers (4+2+4 pairs + 2 cavities)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count is 14, well under 30-layer limit
Multiple cavities require precise thickness control
HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional depositable materials
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for complex stacks
expected_advantages: Sharper passband edges than single-cavity design
More design degrees of freedom for optimization
known_risks: Risk of multiple passband peaks instead of single band
execution_request_english: Design a multi-cavity defect bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack: 4 periods of HfO2/SiO2 (Gao) pairs, one HfO2 cavity layer, 2 periods of SiO2 (Gao)/HfO2 pairs, second HfO2 cavity layer, 4 periods of SiO2 (Gao)/HfO2 pairs. Total 14 layers. Optimize all individual layer thicknesses and both cavity thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Gao).
